NC Word:

An NC word is a single instruction in the CNC program, which is made up of a letter and a number. The letter is called the address, and the number is the value or parameter associated with that address. Each NC word is used to specify a particular function or command for the machine. For example, the NC word "G01" is used to specify linear interpolation, while "M03" is used to start the spindle rotating clockwise.

NC Nodes:

NC nodes are the points along the toolpath where the machine changes direction or speed. These nodes are calculated based on the geometry of the part being machined and the toolpath strategy used. The nodes are used to define the path that the cutting tool will follow during the machining process. Each node is typically defined by a set of coordinates and other parameters that specify the position and movement of the tool.

$$
C_{J_1,J_2} = P(X > Y)
$$

That is, the probability that a randomly selected paper from $ J_1 $ has more citations than a randomly selected paper from $ J_2 $.

This definition is analogous to the **AUC (Area Under the Curve)** metric used in machine learning, which measures the probability that a classifier will rank a randomly chosen positive instance higher than a randomly chosen negative instance. In this context, the AUC is equivalent to the probability that a randomly selected paper from $ J_1 $ has more citations than a randomly selected paper from $ J_2 $, which is the same as the citation success index.

The citation success index can be calculated using the following formula:

$$
C_{J_1,J_2} = \sum_{x=0}^{\infty} \sum_{y=0}^{x-1} P(X = x) P(Y = y)
$$

This formula is similar to the one used to calculate the AUC, where the probability of $ X > Y $ is calculated by summing over all possible values of $ X $ and $ Y $ where $ X $ is greater than $ Y $.
